statements.text: The equation of the straight line with respect to its slope (m) and the y-intercept (b) is y = mx + b, where m ∈ R. Formula: $y = mx + b, \ m \in \mathbb{R}$
Notice that: the equation of the straight line is written ax + by + c = zero, b ≠ 0. Formula: $ax + by + c = 0, \ b \neq 0$

From ax + by + c = 0, by = ax - c, so y = -(a/b)x - (c/b), which is in the form y = mx + c; m = -a/b = -(coefficient of x)/(coefficient of y), and c is the length of the y-intercept. Formula: $y=-\frac{a}{b}x-\frac{c}{b}, \ m=\frac{-a}{b}=\frac{-\text{Coefficient }x}{\text{Coefficient }y}$

context.text: Imagine a water tank that is being filled, and the relation between the time $x$ (in minutes) and the litres $y$ in the tank is $6x - 2y + 40 = 0$. A worker wants to draw this relation as a straight line. Using the equation only, what is the slope of the line and the length of its y-intercept, and how can you use them to draw the line?

Suppose a park map is drawn on a grid. A straight path runs from the gate $A(1, 1)$ to the fountain $B(4, 3)$. The park keeper wants a new straight path through the bench at $(2, 5)$ that meets the first path at right angles. What is the equation of the new path in the form $y = mx + b$?
